plotSections.title: Session Recap and Clarifications
bullets: The party recapped discoveries from the previous session before continuing the story.

The gods' inability to directly interfere with mortals was clarified further: this restriction applies specifically to Elder Gods and Voyager Gods, allowing powerful non-deity entities like Kar to act through the mortal world.
Grixto remains the leading explanation for how Kar is exerting influence over Atlas, acting as Kar's mortal proxy.
The DM clarified that within Atlas, the Abyssal Plane and the Astral Sea are the same location, resolving earlier confusion over the terminology.
The party reviewed the differing accounts of how the Raven Queen rose to power, comparing her own version of events with Vecna's account.
The session officially resumed with the council assembled around the activated Keystone, attended by numerous gods and important allies before any new discussions began.
The party was reminded to level up to level 19.

chronologicalEvents: The group recapped discoveries from the previous session.
The party confirmed that Gerk never owed Ben a bar tab.
The party reviewed that Elder Gods and Voyager Gods cannot directly interfere with mortals, making Grixto the likely means by which Kar acts in the world.
The DM clarified that Kar is not technically a god but an extremely powerful entity comparable to a demon or devil.
The DM clarified that the Astral Sea and Abyssal Plane refer to the same place within Atlas.
The party reviewed the belief that Nevarr may have written himself into one of his own books.
The party discussed the conflicting stories surrounding the Raven Queen's ascension.

The Raven Queen's account was reviewed: she died in battle, met Narul before falling into the Everfalls, accepted his offer, learned to harbor souls, overthrew Narul, and spared him after discovering gods cannot truly be killed.
The party recalled that Vecna's version differed by claiming the Raven Queen had been assassinated and portrayed her far more negatively.
The DM confirmed the Raven Queen's mortal name was Nira.
The DM clarified that only Elder Gods and Voyager Gods are restricted from directly acting upon mortals; lesser divine beings or other powerful entities may not share this limitation.
The party resumed play at the council gathered around the Keystone with the assembled gods and allies.
The DM reminded everyone to advance their characters to level 19.

Kar.existing: A very powerful entity and apparent primary antagonist.
notes: Confirmed not to be a true god despite possessing godlike power.
More accurately described as a powerful entity comparable to a demon or devil.
Can directly interact with mortals because he is not an Elder God or Voyager God.
Likely operates through Grixto as his agent within the mortal world.

Grixto.existing: Proxy of Kar, also known as 'The Enlightened One' or 'The Emperor'.
notes: Continues to be the leading explanation for how Kar influences the mortal world due to the gods' inability to act directly.

Astral Sea.existing: The space around and between the Arches of Atlas.
notes: Confirmed by the DM to be synonymous with the Abyssal Plane within Atlas.
Kar resides within this realm.

Nevarr.existing: Writer and explorer known for his books.
notes: The prevailing theory is that he somehow wrote or narrated himself into one of his books.
His books may provide a means of reaching him if necessary.
openQuestions: Would collecting or using Nevarr's books allow someone to reach him?

Raven Queen.existing: Nira, current goddess of the dead and Elder God.
notes: Her mortal name was confirmed to be Nira.
According to her account, she died in battle before encountering Narul.
Narul offered her a chance to continue existing, and she learned from him how to harbor souls.
She eventually overthrew Narul but spared him after realizing gods cannot truly be killed.
Vecna presents a conflicting version of her rise, including that she was assassinated before meeting Narul.
openQuestions: Which account of her ascension is closest to the truth?

Narul.existing: The Stranger, former Elder God of death.
notes: According to the Raven Queen, he found Nira before the Everfalls and offered her continued existence.
He taught Nira how to harbor souls.
After being defeated by Nira, he was left alive because gods cannot truly be killed.
Confirmed to also be associated with secrets and magic.
Provided a conflicting and more antagonistic account of the Raven Queen's ascension.
Claimed the Raven Queen had been assassinated before becoming a goddess.

Ben.existing: Minor deity who operates the traveling bar and Keeper of the Watchers.
notes: Confirmed that Gerk does not owe him a tab.
Reconfirmed to be the child of Mahali and Nira (not a lich).

Mahali.existing: Elder God and the party's chef.
notes: Reconfirmed to be Ben's father.
Introduced as a class of gods alongside the Elder Gods.
Voyager Gods share the same restriction preventing direct interference with mortals.
openQuestions: What distinguishes Voyager Gods from Elder Gods?

misTranscriptions.notes: Location referenced in the Raven Queen's story.
Clarified to be synonymous with the Astral Sea.

openQuestions: Is Grixto truly Kar's sole method of influencing the mortal world?
Can Nevarr be reached through his books?
Which version of the Raven Queen's ascension is accurate: her account or Vecna's?
What exactly are Voyager Gods, and how do they differ from Elder Gods?

newTerms.name: Voyager Gods
notes: A class of deities distinct from Elder Gods.
They share the restriction against directly interfering with mortals.

newTerms.name: Everfalls
notes: Location where Nira encountered Narul after her mortal death according to the Raven Queen's account.
